issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify Milkable.messageOnMilk() returns a String (and the exercise text says it should return the text "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"), and the template's commented Main code expects a printable return value from messageOnMilk(). However, the solution's Milkable interface and its implementations use boolean messageOnMilk(), printing the message internally and returning a boolean. This return-type mismatch will confuse students about the required method signature and prevents them from returning the expected milk message as a String.
issues.suggestedFix: Make Milkable.messageOnMilk() return String to match the UML and problem description. Update the Milkable interface signature to String messageOnMilk(), and change Seal and Goat implementations to return the formatted string (e.g. "Seal Clarabelle is milked") instead of printing and returning a boolean. Alternatively, if the intent was to return a boolean, update the problem statement and template examples to expect and handle a boolean, but the preferred fix is to align the solution with the stated specification by returning String.

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return a String (the verse text), but the solution repository defines Milkable.messageOnMilk() as returning boolean and the Seal/Goat implementations print the message and return true. This breaks the method contract implied by the UML and Main usage (System.out.println(m.messageOnMilk())), causing students to map the same conceptual operation (milking -> a printable message) to different method signatures and behaviors.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem/template: change Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return String. Update Seal and Goat to implement messageOnMilk() by returning the string "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" (e.g., return "Seal " + getName() + " is milked";) instead of printing and returning boolean. Ensure callers (like Main) print the returned String.
